title: Motion CSV Avg_Disp_*/Max_Disp_Mag became displacement (0 at t=0), but the impact report still reads them as part centroid position and impactor radius
mechanism: a9895c5 (2026-08-11) changed MotionAnalyzer.cpp:173-175 to `dx = displacements[..] - initial_coords_[..]`, so writeMotionCSV (examples/unified_analyzer.cpp:72-93) now writes Avg_Disp_X/Y/Z = 0 and Max_Disp_Mag = 0 on the t=0 row. I checked this on a real deck: the first row is all zeros. The impact consumers were last changed on 07-10 and still assume the old meaning. physics.py:109-115 does `cx = float(dx_arr[0]) ... iz = _impact_z(pos_id)` (which is `pz[0]` of the impactor trajectory, also 0) and then `r_mm = sqrt((px-cx)^2+(py-cy)^2+(iz-cz)^2)`. loader.py:1617-1619 sets `traj.pos_x = list(pm.disp_x)`, and loader.py:1695-1696 builds `ImpactPosition(x=float(traj.pos_x[0]), y=float(traj.pos_y[0]))`. loader.py:686-702 (`_bbox_from_d3plot_part`) returns the first row where `Max_Disp_Mag > 0` as the 'bounding radius', and loader.py:1581-1584 applies it when step_config has no geometry.
scenario: DOE impact at location (20,-15). Part A centroid is at (5,3,1.2) and part B at (-30,10,0.5). Old CSVs gave r_A=23.6 mm and r_B=55.9 mm. New CSVs give cx=cy=cz=iz=0, so r = 25.0 mm for every part, and v_app = 25/Δt ignores part geometry. For a centre impact at (0,0), r_mm=0 and every sample hits `if r_mm <= 0: continue`, so the s8 wave-speed panel shows its placeholder. In the single-d3plot path every position is placed at (0,0). In a KooChainRun DWI run (no step_config.txt), the impactor radius becomes the first non-zero Max_Disp_Mag, e.g. 0.511 mm at t=1e-4 in /data/ball_drop_test_v7/ex01 instead of the mesh radius, and the ρ·V mass fallback drops by about (0.5/8)^3.
consumers: koo_impact_report: s8_physics 'v_app = r/Δt' panel (per-part median/q25/q75 wave speed), impact position map for single-d3plot reports, impactor geometry/mass when step_config geometry is absent. Runs analyzed with a pre-08-11 binary (e.g. /data/koopark/Test_Impact_A/deep_reports, whose t=0 Avg_Disp_X is 26.5) still carry the old meaning, so a campaign that mixes old and new runs mixes the two definitions.
suggested_fix: Stop inferring geometry from motion CSV row 0. Either add explicit Centroid0_X/Y/Z and BoundingRadius0 columns (or JSON fields) in writeMotionCSV, or compute part centroids and impactor extent from the mesh/keyword. Update physics.py, loader.py:1617/1695 and _bbox_from_d3plot_part, and bump the output schema so old and new CSVs are not mixed.

title: stress_ts is built from the 20-sample truncated analysis_result.json arrays and plotted as the real stress history; the peak is missing
mechanism: _extract_part_stress_strain -> _series_to_lists(ts) walks `ts.data`, which koo_deep_report `_parse_series` already filtered with `data = [d for d in raw.get("data", []) if isinstance(d, dict)]` (d3plot_reader.py:564), so the "...(omitted 972 entries)..." marker disappears. The loader never compares len(data) with the JSON `num_points` (992), and it never reads the full-resolution stress/part_<id>_von_mises.csv that sits next to the JSON. The result is stored as `rec["stress_times"]/["stress_max_series"]` (loader.py:1235-1236) and becomes PairResult.stress_ts (loader.py:1713-1716). _ts_payload (payload/__init__.py:103-118) sends it out, and the JS labels it 'Real stress time-series'. This is the consumer side of known item (a); it stays broken even after the C++ writer is fixed (see the stale-reuse finding).
scenario: Production Test_Impact_A, F5_DOE_013 (Run_20260603_075506_fe0239), part 21 Display: JSON global_max=2255.42 at time_of_max=4.847e-05 s, but data has only t in [0, 9.08e-06] and [9.918e-04, 1.0e-03]. Payload stress_ts has n=20 and max=201.47; the true peak (11x larger) is absent. The polyline draws a straight line from 9.08e-6 to 9.918e-4, so the whole impact pulse is invisible. Every one of the 625 results in impact_payload.json has a 20-point stress_ts.
consumers: s2_inspector._renderTimeHistory (ii-th-svg), s3_verdict.renderTSGrid (top-12 stress mini charts labelled with the true peak fmt(r.s) next to a curve that never reaches it), impact_payload.json sidecar (--from-json re-render).
suggested_fix: Treat `len(data) < num_points` (or any non-dict entry) as truncated: load stress/part_<id>_von_mises.csv, or set stress_ts=None with a load_issue. Do not silently drop the marker in _parse_series. Note that the strain CSVs also use fixed 6 decimals, so strain must not take the CSV route.

title: Parts or runs with no motion CSV or stress history are emitted as measured peak_g/peak_disp/peak_stress = 0, and a failed unified_analyzer run becomes an all-zero position with no load_issue
mechanism: load_per_part_motions returns `{}, None` on any unified_analyzer failure (loader.py:1104, 1119-1120) and only prints. load_single_d3plot_report continues and builds PairResults for every keyword part: `peak_g=float(pm.peak_g) if pm else 0.0`, `peak_disp=float(pm.peak_disp) if pm else 0.0`, `peak_strain=float(ss.get("peak_strain", 0.0) or 0.0)` (loader.py:1722-1730). Nothing is appended to load_issues. In the DOE merge, `n_failed = len(runs) - sum(1 for s in sub_reports if s is not None and s.results)` (loader.py:2512) does not count it as failed. The sub-report is also cached (.impact_cache).
scenario: (1) Production: part 23 (beam damper 'DamperSetion', not in analysis_result analyzed_parts) appears in all 25 positions with g=0.0, s=0.0, d=0.0, and the verdict table lists it as a 'PASSED' part. (2) Reproduced by monkeypatching load_per_part_motions to ({}, None), simulating a unified_analyzer OOM or missing binary, on Run_20260603_075506_fe0239 (a contact run, glstat impact_visible=True): 25 results with peak_g=0.0 and peak_disp=0.0 for every part, load_issues=[], trajectory n_states=0.
consumers: payload results g/s/e/d, kpi (n_safe, worst), analyzer findings/outlier gate, safe_drop_zone (position counted safe), doe peak_g_matrix/heatmaps/IDW, PCA, corr network, verdict table, impact_report.json.
suggested_fix: Use None, not 0.0, for parts without motion/stress (the loader already does this for s1/s3/e1/e3/evm). When load_per_part_motions returns no motions, record a 'motion-extraction-failed' load_issue, count the run as failed in n_failed, and skip caching it.

title: peak_stress silently falls back to matsum peak internal energy (mJ), which is then labelled and compared as stress (MPa)
mechanism: `peak_stress = float(ss.get("peak_stress", 0.0) or 0.0); if peak_stress <= 0.0 and matsum and p.part_id in matsum.part_ids: ... ies = [row[idx] for row in matsum.internal_energy]; peak_stress = max(ies)`. No flag records the substitution (models.py only has a comment). The value goes into PairResult.peak_stress, and the payload writes it as `"s"` with unit_labels.stress='MPa'.
scenario: Reproduced with stress_strain empty (the unified_analyzer failure above) on Run_20260603_075506_fe0239: part 1 peak_stress=20.9567 (matsum IE, mJ), part 2=0.04365, part 4=0.000283. The report shows these as MPa stresses. The same path triggers for any part with no von Mises history but nonzero IE, such as discrete/beam damper parts in DampingSpring decks or a part missing from stress_history.
consumers: kpi.worst_s (s1 WORST STRESS tile), analyzer 'stress exceeds yield' CRITICAL finding and SF text, DI composite, failure_risk ranking/SF matrix, safe_drop_zone stress threshold (P75), IDW peak_stress surface, s9 per-part table.
suggested_fix: Remove the proxy, or store it in a separate field (e.g. peak_ie) with its own unit. Leave peak_stress None when no stress history exists.

title: rcforc contact mask uses a per-interface relative threshold, so noise-only interfaces mark 'contact' and set t_first_contact on runs where nothing touched
mechanism: _compute_contact_mask: for each interface `peak = max(fmag)`, `thresh = max(peak_ratio * peak, baseline_multiplier * baseline)` and then `if fmag[lo] > thresh: mask[ti] = True`. There is no absolute or global floor and no filtering to interfaces involving the impactor, so an interface whose whole signal is 1e-2 N of noise still crosses 10% of its own peak. When no side==-1 rows exist, both sides are used (`candidates = totals if totals else list(rcforc_list)`). _compute_trajectory_summaries then takes t_first_contact and z_ref from this mask (loader.py:419-425).
scenario: Production F5_DOE_001, a glstat no-contact run (Run_20260603_070054_0e82f4): every rcforc interface has peak |F| <= 1.397e-02 N (contact runs reach 34-760 N), yet ids 116/143 exceed their own 10% threshold at t=5e-6 s. Payload: trajectories.F5_DOE_001.t_first_contact=1e-06, 79 'contact' samples, max_pen=4.90 mm (free-flight travel reported as penetration). doe.advanced.toa has entries for all 25 positions including the 16 no-contact runs (e.g. DOE_001 'PKG 8 dt_ms 0.001'), and mean_arrival_per_part is averaged over n_positions=25.
consumers: trajectories.t_first_contact/max_pen, part_motion.t_first_contact (global marker), doe toa (earliest/latest part, s9 FIRST ARRIVAL KPI and TOA column), s5 contact-sequence timeline (CONTACT cells on no-contact runs), trajectory_summary.n_contact_steps, max_penetration_depth.
suggested_fix: Apply a global floor, e.g. relative to the maximum interface peak across all interfaces or to impactor KE/v0 scale. Consider only interfaces that involve the impactor part (contact_map). Skip TOA for behavior_class=='no-contact'.

title: A single global t_first_contact taken from the first trajectory is drawn as the 'impactor first contact' marker for every position
mechanism: `for tr in trajectories.values(): tfc = tr.get("t_first_contact"); if tfc is not None and tfc > 0: t_first_contact = float(tfc); break` -> part_motion_payload['t_first_contact']. s9_position.py:470 `const tfc = (DATA.part_motion || {}).t_first_contact;` draws it on the selected position's acceleration chart. s4_part_g.py:283-290 draws it with the label 't₁ = ...' on the per-part chart, whose curves come from arbitrary positions.
scenario: Production payload: part_motion.t_first_contact=1e-06 comes from F5_DOE_001, a no-contact run whose value is itself noise. Actual per-position values are F5_DOE_013=1e-05 and F5_DOE_014..025=5e-06. Selecting F5_DOE_013 in s9 draws the first-contact line at 1 µs instead of 10 µs.
consumers: s9 per-position acceleration chart marker, s4 per-part G chart marker and 't₁' label.
suggested_fix: Emit t_first_contact per pos_id (e.g. part_motion.t_first_contact_by_pos) and look it up with the selected posId in s9 and s4. Exclude no-contact trajectories.

title: Verdict table strain column uses toFixed(4), so realistic device strains of 1e-5 display as 0.0000
mechanism: `el('td', { class: 'num' }, r.e.toFixed(4))` for the worst-G row of each part. The same fixed format appears in analyzer.py:248 CRITICAL finding detail `ε={worst.peak_strain:.4f}`.
scenario: Production impact_payload.json: 12 of 25 parts show '0.0000', e.g. PKG\SUBPKG e=2.532e-05, PKG\PKG 2 e=5.4e-06, PKG\PKG 8 e=8.69e-06. PKG 10 (5.15e-05) and Motor (7.49e-05) round to '0.0001'.
consumers: s3 Verdict table (per-part ε column); findings detail text when --threshold-critical is used.
suggested_fix: Use the magnitude-aware fmt(), or toExponential as in s9_position.py:292, and in analyzer use `{:.3g}`.

title: Contact/peak times are multiplied by 1000 (ms), rounded to 2 decimals, and labelled with the solver time unit 's'
mechanism: s4: `'t₁ = ' + (pm.t_first_contact * 1000).toFixed(2) + (_u('time') ? ' ' + _u('time') : '')`. The x-axis ticks are `(tv * 1000).toFixed(2)` under the axis label `'t  (' + _u('time') + ')'` (s4_part_g.py:254-257). s5_doe.py:943 does the same: `['t₁ CONTACT', (tr.t_first_contact * 1000).toFixed(2) + ' ' + _u('time')]`. unit_labels.time is 's' for ton-mm-s.
scenario: Production (units ton-mm-s, time label 's'): F5_DOE_014 t_first_contact=5e-06 s shows 't₁ CONTACT 0.01 s', and F5_DOE_013 (1e-05 s) shows the same '0.01 s', a 2000x overstatement with two distinct times made identical. The global value 1e-06 in s4 shows 't₁ = 0.00 s'. Axis ticks read 0.00..1.00 under 't (s)' for a 1 ms record.
consumers: s4 per-part G chart axis and t₁ label; s5 trajectory inspector KPI 't₁ CONTACT'.
suggested_fix: Label as 'ms' only when the solver time unit is s, otherwise leave unscaled. Use toFixed(3) or toPrecision(3) so µs-scale contact times stay distinguishable.

title: Reuse of existing deep_report output has no staleness check, and the .impact_cache fingerprint ignores the unified_analyzer and loader version
mechanism: `_reuse = ((work_dir / "analysis_result.json").exists() and (work_dir / "motion").is_dir() and any(...glob("part_*_motion.csv")))`. It checks existence only: no comparison of d3plot mtime against analysis_result.json, and no producer version (metadata.kood3plot_version is constant '1.0.0'). Binout/glstat are then read fresh from the run dir. _run_fingerprint (loader.py:2170-2197) hashes only schema/caps, d3plot/glstat/binout0000 stat, deep json/motion stat and cfg, with no binary or package version and no keyword file.
scenario: (1) After the C++ fix for known item (a) is deployed, existing deep_reports/<run>/analysis_result.json (Test_Impact_A: all 25 truncated) keep being reused. The post_analyze skip-existing batch never regenerates them, so stress_ts stays at 20 points indefinitely. (2) For runs without deep_dir (KooChainRun DWI layout), the first report caches sub.pkl in <test_dir>/.impact_cache/v6 (present in production). A rerun after deploying a new unified_analyzer returns 'cache: N/N hit' with the old truncated series until someone bumps _CACHE_SCHEMA or passes --refresh-cache. (3) If a run is re-solved in place (rerun.sh), the new d3plot/binout are newer than the reused analysis_result.json, and one position mixes old peak_g/stress/motion with new energy_flow/solver_quality.
consumers: All PairResult peaks, stress_ts, part_motions, trajectories for affected runs, and every payload section built from them.
suggested_fix: Reuse only when analysis_result.json mtime >= d3plot mtime and the JSON is not truncated (num_points == len(data)). Include the unified_analyzer binary identity (path+mtime or build hash), the koo_impact_report/koo_deep_report versions and the keyword file stat in _run_fingerprint.

title: Motion CSV Time is written with fixed 6 decimals (1 µs); with output intervals below 1 µs the loader gets duplicate timestamps, and FFT/SRS/t_peak are off by the interval ratio
mechanism: Writer examples/unified_analyzer.cpp:78 `ofs << std::fixed << std::setprecision(6) << point.time`. The loader reads it directly with `pm.times.append(fv("Time"))` and never checks for non-increasing time. _fft_dominant_freq (analytics.py:24-31) uses `dts = dts[dts > 0]; dt = mean(dts)`. SRS uses median of positive dts and np.interp over duplicate x. The same Time feeds t_peak_g, TOA and stress-wave velocity. Displacements are also quantized to 1e-6 (1 µm in SI decks).
scenario: Output interval 1e-7 s over 2 ms: the 20000 states collapse to 2001 unique times. Reproduced with analytics._fft_dominant_freq: a 20 kHz acceleration signal reports f_dom=20000 Hz with true times and 2000.0 Hz with the CSV-quantized times (fs 1e7 -> 1e6). With the production 1.008e-6 interval, times carry up to 0.5 µs error, e.g. t_first_contact values of exactly 5e-06/1e-05.
consumers: deep_analytics.fft (dominant frequency, spectrum), srs, part_motion.t_peak_g, toa dt_ms, stress_wave_velocity, part_motion t_ref charts.
suggested_fix: Write Time with std::scientific/setprecision(9), as the surface CSV already does at line 175. In the loader, detect non-strictly-increasing times and flag them rather than feeding FFT/SRS.

title: Impactor density is rounded to 6 decimals, so the ton/mm³ density shows as 0 in the part drill-down material card
mechanism: `"impactor_material": {"youngs_modulus": round(imp_youngs, 4), "density": round(imp_density, 6)}`, rendered by s6_deep.py `['충격체 밀도', fmt(mat.density, 6)]` when the part has no yield (has_yield False).
scenario: Production Test_Impact_A: meta.impactor.density=7.85e-09 but deep_analytics.per_part_drilldown.impactor_material.density=0.0. Every part has no yield (ELASTIC), so the card shows impactor density '0.000000' for all parts. A kg/mm³ deck (7.85e-06) also collapses to 0.0.
suggested_fix: Use _r4 (significant figures) or no rounding for density.

title: KPI worst_s is rounded to 1 decimal, so GPa-unit stresses collapse and the stress-limit comparison uses the rounded value
mechanism: `"worst_s": round(max(s_vals) if s_vals else 0.0, 1)`. s1_overview.py:265 `fmt(k.worst_s, 1)` and s1_overview.py:217 `if (sv && (k2.worst_s || 0) > k2.stress_limit) sv.style.color = 'var(--crit)'`. html_report.py:145 SSR `f"{kpi['worst_s']:.0f}"`.
scenario: A kg-mm-ms/GPa deck with a true worst stress of 0.0863 GPa shows WORST STRESS '0.100' (+16%), 0.04 shows '0.0', and SSR shows '0'. With --stress-limit 0.09, 0.0863 rounds to 0.1 > 0.09 and the tile turns red although the limit is not exceeded. The Test_Impact_A no-contact-only subset has worst stress 0.1357, which would show as 0.1.
consumers: s1 WORST STRESS KPI tile and its stress-limit colouring; SSR page-1 hero.
suggested_fix: Keep full precision in the payload (or use _r4) and format only in JS.

title: Damage Index reads yield via getattr on a dict, so yield-based DI is never used and the panel silently shows the composite score
mechanism: `sim_params = getattr(report, "sim_params", None)` (a dict) then `ym = getattr(sim_params, "yield_stress_by_part", None) or {}`, which is always {}, so `has_yield` is always False and every part gets `"di_source": "composite"`. The yield branch would also crash on `int(peak_pos)` for string pos_ids like 'F5_DOE_001'. The same getattr-on-dict pattern for grid appears at insights.py:359 and :946.
scenario: A deck with *MAT_PLASTIC_KINEMATIC (keyword parser fills sim_params['yield_stress_by_part'] = {pid: SIGY}) and peak_stress 1.8x yield at several positions: DI should be the sum of (σ/σy - 1) with source 'yield', but the panel shows a normalized composite in [0,1] with source 'composite'.
consumers: s7 Damage Index panel (DI values, ranking, top pairs, summary.has_yield); auto_recommend DI text.
suggested_fix: Use `(sim_params or {}).get("yield_stress_by_part")` and `_pid_cast(peak_pos)` for the pos id.

title: DOE discovery silently skips runs without step_config.txt or without d3plot/deep output, and the report never knows they existed
mechanism: `if not cfg_path.exists(): continue` (1987) and `if not d3plot.exists() and deep_dir is None: continue` (1990, same at 2065/2098). No warning and no load_issue. load_partial_impact_doe_report sets `n_runs=len(runs)` and `n_failed` only from discovered runs, and does not compare against scenario grid nx*ny (read only as a hint at 2596-2604) or jobs.json.
scenario: A 5x5 DOE where 2 jobs are still pending/cancelled (Run dir with step_config but no Output/d3plot yet) or whose Output was cleaned: the report shows n_positions=23 and 'Runs failed to load' is absent. KPIs, safe-zone counts and the 'n_valid_runs 9/23' badge describe 23 runs as the whole DOE, and grid cells for the missing positions are just empty.
consumers: kpi.n_positions/n_safe, analyzer findings (n_runs denominators), DOE grid/heatmaps, impact_report.json doe_config.n_runs.
suggested_fix: Record skipped Run_* dirs as load_issues (kind 'run-skipped' with reason) and count them in n_runs/n_failed. Warn when discovered positions != grid nx*ny.

title: Tier C (101-300 positions) keeps energy flows and acceleration curves for only the top 40 positions with no chunks and no notice; the energy panel silently keeps the previous position
mechanism: `if _topk > 0 and len(_ef_items) > _topk: ... _ef_items = _ef_items[:_topk]` and `_topk_pos = ...[:_tier.part_motion_topk]` (lines 488-495), with tier C emit_mode 'deferred', so emit.py writes no chunk files. s3_verdict.py:830 `if (!flows[posId]) return;   // 흐름 없는 위치면 현 상태 유지`. s9 shows 'no acc time series' for positions outside the top 40. No JS text mentions the cap.
scenario: A 150-position DOE: selecting the 41st-ranked position in s9 leaves the energy graph/Sankey/conservation panels showing the previously selected position's flow, and the acceleration chart says the series does not exist although it was computed and dropped.
consumers: s3 energy-flow panels, s9 per-position charts, s4 per-part G chart.
suggested_fix: Write chunks for tier C too, or clear the panel with an explicit 'dropped by tier cap (top-40)' message. Add the cap to the payload meta and show it.

title: Contact-sequence timeline hard-codes a 0-1 ms time axis and samples only 21 indices of the contact mask
mechanism: Header `(i % 5 === 0) ? (i / 20).toFixed(1) : ''` and cell title `'t=' + (i / 20).toFixed(2) + ' ms'` (line 747) regardless of the trajectory's actual t, while cells take `idx = Math.floor(i * (T - 1) / 20)` from the downsampled contact array.
scenario: Test_DropWeight_Validation (tFinal=0.002 s) and fullangle decks (0.005 s): a contact at 1.5 ms is shown under the '0.8 ms' label, and Test_DWI (tFinal 0.5 ms) is stretched to '1.0 ms'. A contact shorter than record/20 (e.g. 40 µs in a 1 ms record) can fall between sampled indices and show 'free flight'.
suggested_fix: Derive labels and cell times from tr.t (t0..t_end in the declared unit). Mark a cell engaged if any sample in its time bin is engaged (OR over the bin) instead of point-sampling.
